title: Ze’iri (I)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rabbi Chiyya’s student, as stated explicitly in Shabbat 156a: “It is written in Ze’iri’s notebook: I said before Rabbi — and who is it? Rabbi Chiyya.”

He was Rav’s colleague, as we find their disputes in Bava Kamma 30b and Gittin 24b. He was in the Land of Israel even after Rav went down to Babylonia, as in Chullin 106a: when Rabbi Elazar went up, he found Ze’iri and said to him, “Who is the reciter here who taught Rav [the laws of] the udder?” He showed him Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avdimi; and so it is in Bava Batra 87a, except that there it reads “whom Rav taught.” He disagrees with Rabbi Yannai, as in Menachot 9b.
We find at the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim, chapter 9: Rabbi Yochanan in the name of Rabbi Ze’irah; Hyman considers Ze’iri undoubtedly correct.

Likewise what we find in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, beginning of halakhah 2 of chapter 7, and Shevuot 2:4, “Rabbi Ba bar Mamal before Rabbi Ze’ira,” there too Hyman proposes Ze’iri, for Rabbi Zeira was like a student to Rabbi Abba bar Mamal.

Afterward he went down to Babylonia, as we find in Berakhot 22a: “When Ze’iri came, he said: They abolished the immersion.” Hyman states that he spread Torah in Babylonia and that all the great students of Rav and Shmuel received from him too.
Rav Yehudah said that Ze’iri said: Menachot 21a, Avodah Zarah 61b.
Rav Giddel said that Ze’iri said: Menachot 21a.

Rav Acha bar Ashi was his student, as in Yoma 77b: “Rabbi Yitzchak bar bar Chana said: I saw Ze’iri, who went to Rav Chiyya bar Ashi his student.” In Shabbat 109a and 140a, Ze’iri’s wife prepared [food] for Chiyya bar Ashi and he did not eat; she said to him: “For your teacher I prepared it and he ate, and you do not eat?”
Rav Chisda said that Ze’iri said: Berakhot 43a, 31a, 49b and 60b.
In Ketubot 13a he disagrees with Rav Assi.

In Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 6:1, “Rabbi Ba bar Zavda asked before Rabbi Ze’ira”; Hyman proposes “before Ze’iri.” Of his personal life we find in Berakhot 18b that once he deposited zuz with his hostess; while he came and went to the study house, she died. He went after her to the court of death, etc. Since the Gemara places the incident of Ze’iri before that of Shmuel’s father, Hyman infers that it refers to the first Ze’iri.

Sanhedrin 67b relates that once he came to Alexandria in Egypt and bought a donkey; when he came to water it, it dissolved, and there stood a landing-plank. They said to him: “Were you not Ze’iri, we would not return [your money] to you.”

notes.text: כחל means udder, not eye-salve. Returned Davidson Chullin110a matches the supplied106a quotation, while BavaBatra87a contrasts who taught Rav with whom Rav taught; preserve the change of subject. In Yoma77b Ze’iri initially visits his student, with RavAshi’s opposite version separately present in that witness. Acha versus Chiyya barAshi remains Hyman’s heading/quotation difference. גמלא דוסקניתא remains landing-plank. His Ze’ira/Ze’iri identifications remain proposed.

The consulted Chullin 110a asks who taught Rav the udder laws, while Bava Batra 87a asks whom Rav taught measures; supplied 106a is retained. Yoma 77b first has Ze’iri visit Chiyya bar Ashi, then gives Rav Ashi’s opposite version. Hyman’s Acha/Chiyya forms and Ze’ira/Ze’iri emendations remain distinct. His migration, all-great-students and narrative-order dating claims are not independently established by these passages.
